content.text: A non-streaming Claude API call sends nothing back until the whole response is finished, and for a long output that silence is the problem: networks drop idle connections, and the SDK times out and starts over. content.text: The half-truth: for a short request, the difference really is mostly about how the text appears. But the two calls use the connection differently, and that difference grows with the length of the response.
A non-streaming call is one long silence
, the API sends the response when the last token is generated. Until then the HTTP connection carries nothing. A long output takes time to generate: Claude Opus 5.5 accepts

up to 128K, and its adaptive thinking is always on, so it can also spend part of that time reasoning before the first word. The docs list what silence does on real networks: "Some networks might drop idle connections after a variable period of time, which can cause the request to fail or time out without receiving a response from Anthropic."
The Python SDK protects you in three ways. Requests time out after 10 minutes by default. It raises a
"if a non-streaming request is expected to take longer than approximately 10 minutes"; the thinking docs put that line at a

above 21,333 and call it "a client-side validation, not an API restriction". And when a request outlives its timeout, the client ends the connection and retries "without receiving a response". That retry is a new request, so the generation starts again from the beginning.

content.text: , but it doesn't make the connection any less idle. A proxy or load balancer can still drop it, and when the longer timeout expires, the SDK's default two retries can each start the whole generation again before the error reaches your code.

A stream can still be cut off by the network. For Claude 4.6 and later models, the docs' recovery is to keep what you received, then send a new request with a user message that contains the partial response and asks Claude to continue where it left off. Putting the partial text in an assistant turn, the older approach, is a prefill, and Claude 4.6 and later models reject it with a 400. Only text resumes this way: "Tool use and thinking blocks cannot be partially recovered."
